correctness.rationale: Reconstructed RESULT.md lines 60–194 in exact arithmetic. The fixed-point quadratic has product -qr/h² and sum q-(1-a²)r/h². Since p>q and h²p+r=a²rp/(p-q)>a²r, and h²p+r>r, the projective multiplier ρ lies strictly between zero and one. Write t=t(P_n) and Δ=P_{n+1}-P_n. From the inverse φ(t)=(p-mt)/(1-t), the ratio of successive increments is ρ(1-t)/(1-ρ²t), so the second difference divided by Δ is (ρ-1)(1+ρt)/(1-ρ²t). Substituting gives φ(ρ²t²) for the extrapolate wherever defined. For 0<|a|≤1, P₁≥q>(p+m)/2, so -1<ρt<0 for all triples from a lower start: no denominator vanishes, raw iterates increase below p, and squared coordinates give decreasing upper bounds. With h=r=1, P₀=0 and 0<q<a²-1, the second difference is positive and the first extrapolate is -q(q+1)/(a²-1-q), independently verifying sharpness. The formal identity at arbitrary t is understood only away from poles and zero differences. The proof does not cover finite precision, feedback of extrapolates, matrix covariances or over-starts.
